{"comments":[{"id":"ad9d794f-8968-415f-bfb1-8358f6ab9f6f","body":"Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): `CrossAppNode` follows the pattern of the other CrossApp types and gains no space or listing fields. This replaces the field list in the 2026-10-22 Decision comment and the Solution's "Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes", after Marc-Antoine's -1 (2026-10-23).

The schema and relation converters already work this way. Each object carries a `rid`, local ids and the author's local id. Roam relation discovery looks spaces up separately with `getSpaceMap` (`discoverSharedRelations.ts:81`).

Each field a caller reads from `SharedNode` today moves like this:

- `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`: discovery returns the spaces next to the nodes. A caller finds a node's space from the space in its `rid`. The converter sets `rid` on every node.
- `schemaId`: callers resolve the node type by the schema's rid (the node's space and `nodeType`), as relation discovery does with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`.
- `authorId`: `CrossAppNode.authorId` is the author's account local id. Callers look names up by it.
- `directMetadata`: dropped. Its only reader is Obsidian import, for `filePath`, and import reads `filePath` again with each node's content (`importNodes.ts:1767-1774`, `importedNodeContent.ts:51`).
- `title`, `created`, `lastModified`: `content.direct.value`, `createdAt` and `modifiedAt`. `modifiedAt` stays the latest time of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content.

`importedFromRid` stays as it is today: a field Obsidian keeps locally on imported notes, node types and relations. Discovery doesn't read it. Storing it in the database (one source space or several for a schema) is a later design question, not part of this ticket.

PRs, in order:

1. ENG-1985 adds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter.
2. This ticket's first PR: discovery returns `CrossAppNode` and the spaces, and the Roam callers switch.
3. ENG-2045: Obsidian import switches.
4. This ticket's last PR: delete `SharedNode`.

Done When doesn't change: `SharedNode` is removed without loss of functionality.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-25T05:28:01.926Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-25T05:28:01.831Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"b35b996b-7f48-4bdb-b75f-90d6005cf8b8","name":"siddharth yadav"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"930786f0-2e51-468c-91d2-6ef67d90a1fd","body":"I'm -1 on adding spaceId, spaceName, platform etc. to CrossApp. Note how we have not needed this otherwise so far. The supabase function upsert point has the spaceId in its parameters, and should only allow upsert of local concepts. The eventual vercel upsert point should also have the spaceId in the path. Anyway, in the upsert/sync path, we're always bound by the current spaceId as given in the supabaseContext. {"title":"Add a database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter for nodes","description":"## Problem

* <issue id="3fa2047a-8379-4680-8cba-d1732f8afdd3" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1983/define-intermediate-schemas-for-node-relations-and-schemas">ENG-1983</issue> defined the CrossApp types. This ticket covers converting between them and the database.
* Done: the converters from CrossApp types to the database are on main in `crossAppConverters.ts` (<issue id="269a2c3a-2336-4ee7-848c-bed35caac3c6" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2003/add-converter-for-crossappnode-to-localconceptdatainput">ENG-2003</issue>, <issue id="e44234f9-fc2d-4388-9cdc-9059ba06ffe9" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2004/add-converter-for-crossappnode-to-localcontentdatainput">ENG-2004</issue>, <issue id="9e85cfe7-2cfb-4e9a-89cc-8b8ec6ea53bd" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2017/add-converter-for-crossapp-schemas-to-localconceptdatainput">ENG-2017</issue>, <issue id="23a40304-3eea-45bd-ab11-aca36e2f442a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2018/add-converter-for-crossapprelation-schema-to-localconceptdatainput">ENG-2018</issue>). <issue id="4ec82637-0a8f-4239-aecb-e6943361577c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2146/bulk-convert-some-db-structures-to-crossapp-structures-as-needed-for">ENG-2146</issue> added the converters from the database to CrossApp types for schemas and relations in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
* Missing: nothing converts database rows to `CrossAppNode`. Discovery builds `SharedNode` by hand instead (`buildSharedNodes` in `sharedNodes.ts`). <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> needs this converter to return `CrossAppNode` from discovery and remove `SharedNode`.

## Solution

* Add a converter from database rows to `CrossAppNode`, and its bulk form, next to `dbNodeSchemaToCrossApp` in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
* Cover the fields `CrossAppNode` has on main. <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> adds its new fields to the converter when it adds them to the type.
* Take the rows discovery already reads, with `content.full` optional. `modifiedAt` is the latest `last_modified` of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content, as `lastModified` is today.

**Open decisions**

1. What does the converter do with a row the contract can't represent, such as one with no author, no created date or no core title? Discovery skips some incomplete rows (`sharedNodes.ts:165-195`) but keeps nodes without an author (`sharedNodes.ts:235`), while `CrossAppNode` requires `authorId`. The schema converter throws instead (`dbToCrossAppConverters.ts:105-108`), and in a listing one throw hides every node.

## Done When

* A converter from database rows to `CrossAppNode` exists in `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
* Unit tests cover slots in the same space and across spaces, the latest-of-three `modifiedAt`, and the rule for incomplete rows.

## Out of Scope

* Refactor the existing sync code to use converters.
* Switching discovery and its callers to `CrossAppNode` (<issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue>).

## Notes

* Draft PR <pull-request id="80cf751e-cc19-4454-82e0-12d32572d608" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-1985-define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-df0fd187d781">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1184</pull-request> is obsolete. It targets the <issue id="3fa2047a-8379-4680-8cba-d1732f8afdd3" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1983/define-intermediate-schemas-for-node-relations-and-schemas">ENG-1983</issue> branch and adds converters to the database that main now has in another form, so it can be closed.
* History:
  * 2026-07-01: Marc-Antoine created this ticket. He opened draft PR <pull-request id="80cf751e-cc19-4454-82e0-12d32572d608" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-1985-define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-df0fd187d781">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1184</pull-request> on 2026-07-02.
  * 2026-07-06: Michael on this ticket: "We'll break this into sub PR's to handle only the required converters at this time". In that day's meeting notes, right after this ticket, he typed: "let's only introduce new code only when we need it". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/q5T9hG7i2>)
  * 2026-07-20: Sid planned the database-to-CrossApp getters for <issue id="8d484b94-3f20-4341-866e-3b95315eaa90" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1856/store-source-identity-metadata-for-roam-imported-nodes">ENG-1856</issue> on PR <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>. <issue id="8d484b94-3f20-4341-866e-3b95315eaa90" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1856/store-source-identity-metadata-for-roam-imported-nodes">ENG-1856</issue> was released without a node getter. [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3613796080>)
  * 2026-08-21: <issue id="4ec82637-0a8f-4239-aecb-e6943361577c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2146/bulk-convert-some-db-structures-to-crossapp-structures-as-needed-for">ENG-2146</issue> (PR <pull-request id="e97e2c01-d389-4942-879f-55fec127dec6" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2146-bulk-convert-some-db-structures-to-crossapp-structures-as-8873a9645b6d">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1300</pull-request>, Marc-Antoine) added the converters from the database for schemas and relations.
  * 2026-10-22: Sid decided this ticket builds the converter for nodes, and <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> uses it.","gitBranchName":"eng-1985-add-a-database-to-crossappnode-converter-for-nodes","status":"Backlog","assignee":"Marc-Antoine Parent","project":"Post-V0 Roam–Obsidian sync architecture","relations":{"blocks":[{"id":"ENG-2091","title":"Unify SharedNode and CrossAppNode"}],"blockedBy":[{"id":"ENG-1983","title":"Define intermediate schemas for node, relations and schemas"}],"relatedTo":[{"id":"ENG-1856","title":"Store source identity metadata for Roam imported nodes"},{"id":"ENG-2146","title":"Bulk-Convert some db structures to CrossApp structures as needed for relation discovery"},{"id":"ENG-1986","title":"Refactor Obsidian sync to use the new cross-app schemas"},{"id":"ENG-2416","title":"Research: Test OpenSpec with Milestone 1"},{"id":"ENG-2413","title":"Decide how Roam and Obsidian move onto the CrossApp types"}],"duplicateOf":null},"parentId":"ENG-2413","id":"ENG-1985"}

{"title":"Unify SharedNode and CrossAppNode","description":"## Problem

* We have two types that represent an abstraction of a node, `SharedNode` (`packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts`) and `CrossAppNode` (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). This makes for a larger cognitive surface.
  * `SharedNode` is the discovery listing: what a user sees for the nodes in a shared space. It has no content body.
  * `CrossAppNode` is the write payload, with direct and full content.
* There are aspects of SharedNode that are missing from CrossAppNode:
  * ~~reference_content (missing)~~ Done: <issue id="99bbd340-1a9c-43d7-8251-0fecde588a34" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129/populate-reference-content-from-crossappnode-and-roles-from">ENG-2129</issue> added `slots` to both types.
  * sourceId: unclear. `SharedNode.sourceLocalId` already maps to `CrossAppBase.localId`.
  * directMetadata: the direct Content row's `metadata`, not `literal_content`. Only Obsidian reads it, to get `filePath`.
  * Space and listing fields: `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`, `schemaId` and the decorated `title`. Roam discovery and import use them.
* We have a lot of code that started using the SharedNode and will need refactoring: 8 files in `apps/roam/src`, and Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`importNodes.ts`).

## Solution

* Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes.
* Take the functions that create SharedNodes from database data, and create equivalent functions that create CrossAppNodes instead
  * No such function exists for nodes today. `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` covers schemas and relations only.
* Start using those new functions in the client code
* Remove SharedNodes

**Open decisions**

1. Does discovery return `CrossAppNode`, or do we keep `SharedNode` as a separate listing type? Michael (2026-07-22) and Marc-Antoine (2026-08-03) pointed to `CrossAppNode`. Sid (2026-07-20) described `SharedNode` as a lightweight listing.
2. If discovery returns `CrossAppNode`, do the space and listing fields go into `CrossAppNode`, or into a listing type that wraps it (for example `{ node, space, schemaDbId, directMetadata }`)?
3. What did "sourceId" mean?
   1. Equivalent to sourceLocalId

{"title":"Remove Obsidian's getPublishedNodesForGroups wrapper and read CrossAppNode directly","description":"## Problem

* Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:53`) is a thin wrapper over shared discovery. Its only job is remapping `SharedNode` to the local `PublishedNode` type (`:43`):
  * ISO strings (`created` / `lastModified`) → epoch numbers (`createdAt` / `modifiedAt`)
  * `directMetadata` (`Json`) → extracted `filePath: string | undefined`
* Michael on PR <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "`getPublishedNodesForGroups` is now redundant. It looks like the only thing it is doing is adding `filePath`, which doesn't warrant an entire wrapped function."
* <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> replaces `SharedNode` with `CrossAppNode`. It can't remove `SharedNode` while this wrapper, Obsidian's only reader of shared discovery, still uses it.

## Solution

* Remove the `getPublishedNodesForGroups` wrapper and the local `PublishedNode` type. Have `ImportNodesModal` (and the `ImportableNode` conversion path) read `CrossAppNode` directly, moving the `filePath`-from-`directMetadata` extraction to the single call site that needs it.
* Do this as a sub-issue of <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue>: after <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue> adds the discovery function that returns `CrossAppNode`, and before it removes `SharedNode`. The wrapper is then deleted once, not rewritten and then deleted.

**Open decisions**

1. The import dialog shows author names by the author's database account id (`ImportNodesModal.tsx:130`, `:371-373`; `typeUtils.ts:92-97`). Does `CrossAppNode` carry that id, or does Obsidian look names up by the account's local id? This is one of the three fields in <issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue>'s open question for Marc-Antoine.

## Done When

* `getPublishedNodesForGroups` and the local `PublishedNode` type are gone.
* Obsidian's import path reads `CrossAppNode` directly.
* A manual import in Obsidian lists the same nodes, titles, dates and author names as before. No automated test covers this path.

## Out of Scope

* Changing discovery itself (<issue id="e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091/unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode">ENG-2091</issue>).
* Obsidian sync's write path (<issue id="f1c9f2d5-4eac-47d8-b4a5-a862196ef911" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1986/refactor-obsidian-sync-to-use-the-new-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1986</issue>).

## Notes

  * 2026-07-20: Michael on PR <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "`getPublishedNodesForGroups` is now redundant." {"comments":[{"id":"ad9d794f-8968-415f-bfb1-8358f6ab9f6f","body":"Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): `CrossAppNode` follows the pattern of the other CrossApp types and gains no space or listing fields. This replaces the field list in the 2026-10-22 Decision comment and the Solution's "Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes", after Marc-Antoine's -1 (2026-10-23).

The schema and relation converters already work this way. Each object carries a `rid`, local ids and the author's local id. Roam relation discovery looks spaces up separately with `getSpaceMap` (`discoverSharedRelations.ts:81`).

Each field a caller reads from `SharedNode` today moves like this:

- `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`: discovery returns the spaces next to the nodes. A caller finds a node's space from the space in its `rid`. The converter sets `rid` on every node.
- `schemaId`: callers resolve the node type by the schema's rid (the node's space and `nodeType`), as relation discovery does with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`.
- `authorId`: `CrossAppNode.authorId` is the author's account local id. Callers look names up by it.
- `directMetadata`: dropped. Its only reader is Obsidian import, for `filePath`, and import reads `filePath` again with each node's content (`importNodes.ts:1767-1774`, `importedNodeContent.ts:51`).
- `title`, `created`, `lastModified`: `content.direct.value`, `createdAt` and `modifiedAt`. `modifiedAt` stays the latest time of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content.

`importedFromRid` stays as it is today: a field Obsidian keeps locally on imported notes, node types and relations. Discovery doesn't read it. Storing it in the database (one source space or several for a schema) is a later design question, not part of this ticket.

PRs, in order:

1. ENG-1985 adds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter.
2. This ticket's first PR: discovery returns `CrossAppNode` and the spaces, and the Roam callers switch.
3. ENG-2045: Obsidian import switches.
4. This ticket's last PR: delete `SharedNode`.

content.thinking:
I need to refactor the row logic out of buildSharedNodes into a shared single-row converter and a bulk converter, so buildSharedNodes reuses that same logic instead of duplicating it. I'm now figuring out what input the converter should actually take.

Looking at the existing converters, they accept Concept rows plus lookup maps (space, account, concept, schema), with bulk versions fetching missing maps via a client. The new converter needs to work with discovery's existing row shapes—SharedConcept, SharedContent, and SharedContentSummary—where the full content summary is optional and only affects modifiedAt.

Mapping out CrossAppNode's fields now: localId comes from source_local_id, rid is derived via spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid, and createdAt needs to come from the direct content's created field—though that's nullable while CrossAppNode requires it non-null, so I need to decide whether to skip rows missing created, even though discovery currently keeps those nodes.

I'm checking whether created or author_id can actually be null in practice—likely the underlying Content table enforces NOT NULL even though the generated view types mark everything nullable, but author_id might genuinely be nullable, which would explain why some nodes lack authors and need to be skipped per the open decision. For authorId, I need to figure out which row supplies author_id since the Concept row discovery selects doesn't include it, so it must come from the direct content row instead.

For nodeType, I need to map schema_id to the schema's source local id the same way relation discovery does it, using the concept map to resolve local ids consistently across node and relation conversion.

I should keep discovery's output unchanged in this PR by refactoring the shared row logic out of buildSharedNodes so the two paths can't diverge. The common pieces are validity checks, resource key joining, lastModified computation, rid, and slot resolution, while schemaId, spaceName, spaceUri, platform, title, coreTitle, created, authorId, and directMetadata stay SharedNode-specific — so I'm designing an extraction that produces per-node intermediate records shared by both.

Since SharedNode is slated for removal in the final PR, the shared logic should live in dbToCrossAppConverters.ts with sharedNodes.ts importing from it, so that when buildSharedNodes is eventually deleted, the converter stays intact untouched.

Having buildSharedNodes wrap the CrossApp converter won't work though, since CrossAppNode lacks schemaId, authorId, and directMetadata that discovery needs, and any change to how no-author nodes are handled would alter discovery's output. I need a lower-level shared step instead, so I'm sketching out a single converter function signature that takes the node, direct metadata, timestamps, and lookup maps for space/account/concept, producing a CrossAppNode while throwing on missing author or space.

I'm also designing a bulk version that processes arrays of nodes against direct and full content summaries, skipping and logging any rows that fail conversion rather than throwing. The real fix is pulling the row-matching logic — joining direct/full content by resource key, picking latest timestamp, resolving slots, validity checks — into one shared implementation that both buildSharedNodes and the new converter call, so they can't drift apart. I'm now working out exactly what inputs that shared row logic needs given buildSharedNodes' existing SharedNodeRows shape.

Spaces come through as full rows, and the converter's spaceMap (id to url) can be derived from them. For slot resolution, I'm tracing through how buildSharedNodes uses concepts_of_relation — a computed relationship returning referenced concepts' id, space, and source local id — to decide whether a referenced concept resolves to a local id, a cross-space rid via the spaces lookup, or gets dropped if its space is missing. That matches the optional local-id resolution pattern given a concept map.

Now I'm thinking about factoring this into a shared function in dbToCrossAppConverters.ts that bundles the joined node data (nodes, direct contents, content summaries) per node, though the existing shared types would need to move out of sharedNodes.ts since that file is slated for deletion.

So the input types match discovery's row shapes. I'm sketching an intermediate row structure that bundles the validated node, direct content, space url, rid, timestamps, and slots so both outputs can derive from one shared piece — though that feels like too much intermediate state. A cleaner alternative might be having the single-row converter emit a CrossAppNode directly, with buildSharedNodes layering on the extra db fields like schemaId, spaceId, space metadata, and author id afterward.

But that converter requires an author and throws when missing, while buildSharedNodes needs to keep authorless nodes around, and those can't be mapped through an accountMap since their author_id is null. So I'm breaking down what actually counts as shared row logic: indexing direct and full contents by resource key, validity checks on schema/space/source fields, timestamp normalization with fallback logic, rid computation with skip-on-failure, and slot resolution from reference content and relation concepts — then figuring out what additional fields CrossAppNode needs on top of that, like node type.

Now I'm weighing whether a missing core_title should cause a row to be skipped entirely, since CrossAppNode requires coreTitle as a non-optional string while SharedNode treats it as optional — the open question is whether older rows without a core_title (because the source never published one) should fall back to title or just be dropped per the documented skip-and-log behavior for unrepresentable rows.

The decision resolves this: skip rows without core title or created date too, logging each skip, though the PR text should make this explicit since discovery currently tolerates missing created dates and core titles. I'm now wondering how common these gaps actually are — created is likely non-nullable on Content, and there's a coreTitleBackfill script that may have already ensured most published nodes have a core title, which would make skipping these a non-issue in practice. I want to check the schema nullability for author_id and created, plus what that backfill script actually does.

Now I'm also looking at how content.direct maps back to Content rows in crossAppConverters.ts, to make sure the reverse mapping (fields like scale and metadata) stays consistent with the InlineCrossAppContent shape.

content.thinking:
Roam already handles missing coreTitle by falling back to incomingTitle, so if ENG-1985's bulk converter skips nodes lacking core_title, ENG-2091 risks dropping those nodes from discovery entirely. Since CrossAppNode.coreTitle is required and defined as matching the title unless a format mismatch occurs, I need to figure out the right fallback behavior when core_title is simply absent.

Falling back to the raw title content instead would risk double-decoration issues during Roam materialize, since the format would get reapplied on top of an already-formatted title. Given the ticket's open decision explicitly lists missing core title alongside missing author/created date/schema/space as examples of rows the bulk converter skips and logs, I'll follow that decision and treat missing core_title as a skip case too, consistent with how discovery already handles missing authors.

I'll note this as a consequence for ENG-2091 rather than block ENG-1985 on it, and flag it to sid separately. Created date is NOT NULL on Content, so a null there can only stem from view nullability, which I'll also treat as a skip case. Next I want to look at how Roam's discoverSharedRelations.ts uses getSpaceMap and dbRelationsToCrossApp, since that will shape how I design the ENG-2091 refactor.

# Style Guide

This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.

## TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## UI Guidelines

- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

## Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

## Code comments

Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.

Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.

Before keeping a comment, check:

- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?

I'm now sketching a cleaner structure: one function handles joining and validity checks (schema, space, direct text) to produce a minimal resolved node row, and then each output type maps that row to its own shape — defining the row type that includes the concept and schema_id fields needed downstream.

content.thinking:
I'm weighing whether to only wrap the node rid lookup in a try/catch versus also wrapping the slot computation—since today only node rid errors are swallowed, wrapping slots too would be a subtle behavior change that could let unrecognized slot-space URLs silently skip nodes instead of failing the whole listing. I want to stay faithful to the current error-swallowing scope rather than widen it.

I realize the only edge case is a slot target pointing into a third space whose URL is malformed, which is extremely theoretical since the same table format validates URLs elsewhere. I'll just flag it briefly as a caveat rather than treating it as a real change to discovery's output.

For logging in the bulk converter, I'll warn with the node's space id and local id (since a proper rid may not be derivable yet) plus the failure reason, and leave the sort in buildSharedNodes unchanged. I'm also checking whether there are other null-field edge cases like missing created dates, though since content.created is NOT NULL that path shouldn't actually trigger.

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.

I'm also mapping out which fields Roam callers expect and how they correspond to the converter's output.

The trickier issue is that `rid` is typed as optional on CrossAppBase even though the converter always sets it, and callers treat it as a required key everywhere. I'm weighing options like narrowing the discovery function's return type to guarantee a non-null rid, versus adjusting the converter's return type directly, trying to find the cleanest way to express that guarantee without bloating the shared type.

I also want to check how existing callers handle this — searching for how discoverSharedRelations deals with relation.rid, and tracing how node types get resolved to rids via spaceUri and local id lookups instead of database ids.

I need to check importSharedRelations for how it resolves rid there. Then I'm tracing all the fields each shared node needs: spaceId for querying by space, spaceName and spaceUri for dialog display and reference resolution, platform for content type expectations, title and coreTitle for the node's content, and created timestamp.

Checking lastModified next — it maps to modifiedAt as a Date, but callers expect ISO strings for display, sorting, and materialization, so I'll need to call toISOString() on it. authorId isn't used in Roam, and slots pass through directly. Now the key question is how callers get a node's space — I'm thinking discovery could return nodes and spaces separately, with callers building a map by space URI to look up each node's space.

Based on the decision to have discovery return spaces alongside nodes and derive a node's space from its rid, I'm restructuring calls like materializeSharedNode and importSharedNodes to pass explicit node/space pairs rather than looking things up separately. I'm now defining the SharedSpace type for the discovery API in the database package.

I'm sketching a discovery module that returns both the cross-app nodes and a space lookup keyed by url, so consumers can resolve a node's originating space directly. I'm still working out naming, and noting the old functions will get removed in a later PR anyway.

Since only Roam uses getSharedNodeByRid while Obsidian relies solely on listGroupSharedNodes via getPublishedNodesForGroups, I realize I can just modify getSharedNodeByRid in place to return the richer CrossAppNode-plus-space shape without worrying about breaking Obsidian.

For listGroupSharedNodes though, Obsidian still depends on it until ENG-2045, so I need to add a separate new function for Roam rather than changing it directly. I'm weighing names like listSharedCrossAppNodes for the db-level function, distinct from Roam's existing discoverSharedNodes wrapper, with the old function getting deleted once Obsidian migrates.

I'll leave Obsidian untouched for now and go with `listGroupSharedCrossAppNodes` as the new function name, explicit about returning CrossApp nodes, with the final PR deleting the old `listGroupSharedNodes`. I should grep to double check Obsidian isn't affected, then look at the existing `SharedSpace` type definition to see how it's shaped.

I'm checking whether the existing sort order in buildSharedNodes actually matters, since the dialog re-sorts anyway. Since sortSharedNodes does a stable sort only on lastModified, ties fall back to the input order, so I need to preserve the original title-based tiebreak to keep the dialog's displayed order identical.

For dbNodesToCrossApp, I also need to fetch the account map and schema map via extra client queries, and for Roam the converter still requires authorId even though it's unused there, so I'll keep that skip rule intact. I'm also deciding that getAssociatedSpaces should return all valid spaces for the listed nodes plus slot targets and the current space, since callers look up spaces by each node's rid.

For the space lookup itself, I'm mapping rids to their spaceUri — Obsidian note rids map to a vault-based URI while Roam rids map to the graph's roamresearch.com URL — and matching that against each space's url field. Since materializeSharedNode operates per node and each node could belong to a different space, it makes more sense to pass a `spaces` map keyed by URI rather than a single space. The refresh function can just return node plus space together, and the dialog needs to display and sort by spaceName as a column alongside title and lastModified.

Looking back at the actual decision history, the October 25th resolution landed on CrossAppNode staying unchanged and discovery returning spaces alongside nodes, with callers responsible for resolving a node's space from the rid -- so a local pairing type on the Roam side would mean duplicating that lookup work at the call site.

I'm sketching out a SharedNodeSpace type keyed by url and a getSharedNodeSpace helper that extracts the space from a node's rid, though I'm second-guessing whether the rid field can safely be assumed non-null given that the converter always populates it.

I'm also weighing whether to amend the converter's return type now that ENG-1985 already shipped with a plain CrossAppNode return, versus having downstream signatures declare the rid-required intersection type themselves. Given that, I'm leaning toward having the converter itself guarantee rid is set at the source, narrowing the type right where it's created rather than introducing a new alias.

I'm deciding that discovery functions should return nodes typed as CrossAppNode, consistent with other converters, and that Roam code will use a non-null assertion on rid since the converter always sets it—though with around 15 call sites that's a bit noisy, so I'm weighing whether to reconsider the decomposition instead.

I'm deciding to skip the alias and just type Roam functions as plain CrossAppNode, handling rid presence through validation at each call site rather than a narrowed type. I'll write the code first and see how many non-null assertions pile up — if too many, I'll switch to the narrowed converter type instead, weighing which approach would hold up better in review.

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

### Mobile compatibility

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile
- If the plugin targets mobile, use web API equivalents: `SubtleCrypto` instead of `crypto`, `navigator.clipboard` for clipboard access

- The plugin ships with `isDesktopOnly: false`, so it must load on mobile

```

  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

/**
 * A node type schema's title format lives in two places in the concept's
 * literal_content: the top-level `format` key and `source_data.format`
 * (written by Obsidian). Roam writes the top-level key as of ENG-2158, and
 * ENG-2175 backfills Roam rows published before it.
 *
 * The top-level key is the contract and is always authoritative; the nested
 * key is read only as a fallback. The dual read is temporary and goes away
 * once Obsidian also writes the top-level key (ENG-2208) and existing rows
 * are backfilled.
 */
export const resolveSchemaFormat = ({
  format,
  sourceDataFormat,
}: {
  format?: string | null;
  sourceDataFormat?: string | null;
}): string => format || sourceDataFormat || "";

input.message:
ENG-1985 has a new commit for the core title: 4d255fba "Derive a missing core title from the node type's format", on top of 63dbd5d0. ENG-2091 is restacked on it.

One deviation from your note, for your log: the converter reads the format with resolveSchemaFormat (packages/utils), not literal_content.format alone. resolveSchemaFormat prefers the top-level `format` and falls back to `literal_content.source_data.format`. Reason: Obsidian schemas on main publish their format only under source_data until ENG-2208. With the top-level key alone, an Obsidian node with no core_title would get its full decorated title as coreTitle, and Roam import would decorate it twice. Roam's resolveSharedNodeTypes resolves node-type formats the same way, and packages/database already depends on @repo/utils.

How it works: when core_title is null, coreTitle = extractContentFromTitle(format ?? "", title). With no format, coreTitle is the title. The bulk converter fetches a formatMap (schema id → format) in one extra my_concepts query. The single converter takes formatMap.

Skip rules now: no author, no created date, or a schema the group can't see (no node type), plus discovery's existing skips. Tests cover the derived title, the no-format case, and the format fetch with the source_data fallback.

Checks: eslint, prettier and tsc are clean. ci:validate passes all 8 check-types and all unit tests (database 142). Continuing with ENG-2091's tests.

ENG-2091's first PR is committed locally, not pushed. Branch eng-2091-unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode, worktree .claude/worktrees/eng-2091. Commit 3782117f, on ENG-1985's 4d255fba.

What changed:
- packages/database sharedNodes.ts: new listGroupSharedCrossAppNodes returns SharedNodeListing = { nodes: DbCrossAppNode[]; spaces: Record<url, SharedNodeSpace> }. SharedNodeSpace is { id, name, platform, url }; space validation is shared with buildSharedNodes. getSharedNodeByRid changed in place to return { node, space } | null, since Roam refresh is its only caller. New helpers: getSharedNodeSpace (finds the space from the url in the node's rid; throws if missing, which the listing makes impossible) and getNodeTypeRid (the schema rid in the node's space). Obsidian still uses listGroupSharedNodes and buildSharedNodes.
- dbToCrossAppConverters.ts: DbCrossAppNode = CrossAppNode & { rid: string; modifiedAt: Date }, the converter's return type. It adds no fields; it states what the converter always sets. Without it, about 20 Roam sites would need `rid!` or `modifiedAt` checks.
- Roam (dialog, discoverSharedNodes, sort, import, refresh, materialize, importNodeAssets, resolveSharedNodeTypes) reads the listing. Display, filter and sort use space.name, space.url, content.direct.value and modifiedAt. materialize and importNodeAssets take the node's space. resolveSharedNodeTypes queries schemas by space_id and source_local_id and keys them by schema rid. Its result is unchanged; the query by db id is gone.
- materialize no longer checks the modified time (dead now that it's a Date from the converter). Its test for an invalid time is removed; the canonical-UTC test still runs with a Date.
- refreshImportedNode.ts also switched; it wasn't in your caller list. accessors.ts only imports getRoamMarkdownApi and needed no change.

(b) A node with no core_title gets a derived one, so Roam decorates its title by the node type's format, as it does for nodes that published one.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

### Mobile compatibility

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile
- If the plugin targets mobile, use web API equivalents: `SubtleCrypto` instead of `crypto`, `navigator.clipboard` for clipboard access
- Regex lookbehind assertions are not supported on some mobile — avoid them if possible
- The plugin ships with `isDesktopOnly: false`, so it must load on mobile

- Prefer `async`/`await` over `.then()` chains
- Minimize `console.log` — remove debug logs before shipping
- Do not hardcode styles inline — use CSS classes and Obsidian's CSS variables

Two details it settled: `normalizePath("/")` returns `"/"`, and `TFolder.isRoot()` tests `path === "/"` rather than a null parent.

```
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/Resources/obsidian.asar","utf8");
  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

input.message:
ENG-2045 is committed locally, not pushed. Branch eng-2045-remove-obsidians-getpublishednodesforgroups-wrapper-and-read, worktree .claude/worktrees/eng-2045. Commit b915687a, on ENG-2091's 3782117f.

What changed:
- ImportNodesModal reads listGroupSharedCrossAppNodes. Space name, url and platform come from the listing's spaces via getSharedNodeSpace; the dialog no longer calls getSpaceInfoFromIds, though other import code still uses it. Titles come from content.direct.value. Dates are createdAt/modifiedAt.valueOf(); modifiedAt is still the latest of the three.
- Author names by account local id: a new fetchUserNamesByLocalId(client) reads my_accounts (account_local_id, name) for person accounts. The dialog shows `userNamesByLocalId[id] ?? "user <id>"`, the same fallback as getUserNameById. ImportableNode.authorId and GroupWithNodes.authorIds are now strings. fetchUserNames is still called: it refreshes settings.userNames (keyed by db id), which other views use for imported nodes.
- Removed getPublishedNodesForGroups, PublishedNode, ImportableNode.filePath and the `?? node.filePath` fallback in import. refreshImportedFile ran its own `Content` metadata query only to fill that field, so it's removed too; import reads filePath from the same direct row through my_contents. The test harness's now-unused "Content" branch is removed. The stale types.ts comment that named the wrapper is updated.
- GroupWithNodes.spacePlatform is now required; it always comes from the listing. The "Absent when the space lookup failed" comment is removed.

Behavior notes:
(a) Nodes the converter skips (no author, no created date, schema not visible) are missing from the Obsidian dialog too.
(b) A failed listing shows "Failed to load nodes: <db message>" without the old "Failed to fetch published nodes:" prefix. PostgrestError extends Error, so the message still shows.

Checks: prettier and tsc are clean. ci:validate passes all 8 check-types and all unit tests (obsidian 229, 2 new for fetchUserNamesByLocalId).
eslint --max-warnings 0 on importNodes.ts fails on 4 warnings that are on origin/main in lines this PR doesn't touch: an unsafe any spread at ~500, an unknown in a template literal at ~1101, unused `_node` at ~1679, an unnecessary assertion at ~1977. I left them because fixing them would be an unrelated cleanup (rule 6). Tell me if sid wants them fixed here.

---
name: Build and copy to ticket-specific test dir
description: When in a worktree and user asks to build, copy dist to /mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-XXXX/ (ticket-specific, not a shared folder)
type: feedback
originSessionId: 86523deb-ea7b-482f-a5c4-89e43a8422e1
modified: 2026-07-30T11:40:53.931Z
---
When working in a worktree and the user asks to compile or build, always:
1. Run the build in `apps/roam/`
2. Copy the dist output to `/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-<ticket-number>/`
   - Example: for ENG-1651 → `/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-1651/`

**Why:** Ticket-specific directories let sid test multiple branches side by side without overwriting each other. The old shared `/mnt/data/projects/test-dg-build/` path made it unclear which branch was built.
**How to apply:** Any time the user says "build", "compile", or "copy dist" in a worktree context, derive the ticket number from the branch name and use the ticket-specific path.

**Worktree env gotcha (2026-07-30):** env files are untracked, so worktrees have neither `apps/roam/.env` nor `packages/database/.env.local` — a plain build then bakes NO Supabase URL ("Not using the database" in the build log; "Missing required Supabase environment variables" at runtime). Copy both files from the main checkout and build with `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local`; verify with `grep -c 'http://127.0.0.1:54321' dist/extension.js` → 1. Copy the whole dist (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, package.json included) — tooling like the demo recorder validates the folder.

Claude (and every subagent) must NOT start Roam Desktop, open/log into a Roam graph, run Playwright sessions against Roam, or hit the Local API on its own initiative. Work stays at the code level: implement, typecheck, test, build, copy dist. Live verification is sid's to run — deliver a runbook/checklist instead.

**Why:** sid (2026-08-05, extensionAPI.ai.addTool Phase 0): "are you trying to start a roam graph for the mcp??? don't just do everything from the code pov please nothing else, no subagent is allowed to do that as well." Live app sessions on this machine are sid's domain (same spirit as [[feedback_no_headless_recordings]]).

**How to apply:** When a task needs live Roam evidence (receipts, demos, MCP probes), prepare the build + exact step-by-step instructions and hand off; only interact with a running Roam if sid explicitly starts it and asks.

All four PRs in the discovery chain are committed locally. Nothing is pushed and no PRs are open. I stopped at ENG-1879, which the brief puts out of scope. `pnpm ci:validate` passes on every branch: 8/8 typechecks and every unit test.

| PR | Branch (commits) | Lines changed, excluding tests |
|---|---|---|
| ENG-1985 | `eng-1985-add-a-database-to-crossappnode-converter-for-nodes` (`45638983`, `63dbd5d0`, `4d255fba`) | 492, about 145 of them moved |
| ENG-2091 first | `eng-2091-unify-sharednode-and-crossappnode` (`3782117f`) | 458 |
| ENG-2045 | `eng-2045-remove-obsidians-getpublishednodesforgroups-wrapper-and-read` (`b915687a`) | 173 |
| ENG-2091 last | `eng-2091-remove-sharednode` (`5fcff419`) | 88, almost all deletions |

Each branch is stacked on the previous one. The last one needed its own name because Linear's branch name was already taken by the first ENG-2091 PR. ENG-1985 and the first ENG-2091 PR are over 400 lines, so their PR bodies need a reason they can't be split.

**Calls the orchestrator made for you (logged in its session):**
- **Content-model import:** `ContentType` now comes from `@repo/content-model/constants`. Without this, the Obsidian typecheck failed once Obsidian started reading the CrossApp types. It's a one-line commit of its own on ENG-1985.
- **Missing core title:** nodes without one are kept, and the converter derives one the way publish does. I read the format through `resolveSchemaFormat`, not only `literal_content.format`. Obsidian schemas keep their format under `source_data` until ENG-2208, and reading only the top-level key would make Roam decorate those titles twice.
- **Lint warnings:** four existing eslint warnings in Obsidian's `importNodes.ts` are left alone. CI only checks lines a PR adds, and none of them are on ENG-2045's lines.

**My own calls, worth a look in review:**
- **Type:** the converter returns `CrossAppNode & { rid: string; modifiedAt: Date }`. It adds no fields; it states what the converter always sets. Without it, about 20 Roam call sites would need non-null assertions.
- **Refresh lookup:** `getSharedNodeByRid` was changed in place to return `{ node, space }`, since Roam's refresh is its only caller.
- **Dead checks removed:** materialize no longer validates the modified time, which is now always a valid `Date`. Obsidian's refresh no longer runs a separate query just to get `filePath`; import already reads it with the node's content.

**What users will see differently:**
- Both import dialogs no longer list nodes with no author, no created date, or a node type the group can't see. Each skipped node is logged in the console.
- A node published without a core title now has its title decorated by its node type's format, like every other node.

**Before you test:** this checkout's first install of the ENG-2091 branch pulled in the wrong React types. The ui, website and Obsidian typechecks then failed on JSX errors that had nothing to do with this code. Deleting `node_modules` and reinstalling from the same lockfile fixed it. If you see those errors on a fresh checkout, reinstall.

**Manual check for you** (I didn't build or launch anything). Compare origin/main `67e93a0d` with `.claude/worktrees/eng-2091-last`, which contains all four PRs. For each, copy `apps/roam/.env` and `packages/database/.env.local` from the main checkout, then run `pnpm build` in `apps/roam` and in `apps/obsidian`.

In Roam, run "DG: Import shared nodes":
1. The rows are the same: source space name and URL, title, and modified time. The "N of M nodes" count also matches, apart from the skipped nodes above.
2. Search by a space name, part of a URL, and part of a title gives the same results.
3. Sorting each column in both directions gives the same order.
4. Import one Roam node and one Obsidian node: the page titles and node types are the same as before. For a node type that doesn't exist locally, the one created has the same name and format as before.
5. Import a node whose Source isn't imported yet: the Source comes in first and the title includes it.
6. Refresh on an imported page says "Refreshed … from <space>".

In Obsidian, run "Import nodes from another space":
7. The same spaces, titles and counts appear, with real author names (not "user …").
8. Importing one node lands in the same folder, with the same dates, links and assets as before.
9. Refreshing that file from the discourse context view still works.

When you say push, I'll open each PR with the template and then run `/pre-pr-review` and scope-check, as the brief requires. Each PR still needs its Loom.

description: "pre-pr-review must be a separate, independent pass over the real PR diff — an implementer's self-review doesn't count, and follow-up commits need a re-run"

When sid says "use the pre-pr-review skill before PR", run `/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md` as its own read-only pass (a fresh Opus agent per PR, against `gh pr diff N` plus the worktree) after implementation is done, and again after any follow-up commit. The implementing agent saying "I reviewed it" is not the review.

**Why:** On 2026-08-23 sid asked "for each of the pr you did .. did you do the pre-pr-review" for #1330/#1331/#1332; only self-reviews had run. Independent passes then found real defects the implementers missed: a producer key (`author_uid` vs `author_local_id`) that would have blanked `author_id` across the published corpus, a stale legacy-store cache after type creation, and a lossy `{Source}` decoration. See [[project-review-system-v2]].

---
name: Don't rubber-stamp agent refactors
description: When reviewing other agents' (Codex etc) code changes, apply the same critical lens as for own code — reject unnecessary refactors
type: feedback
---

When reviewing changes from Codex or other agents, don't say "Good" or "Correct but invasive" and move on. Apply the same standards:

- **Is the root cause already fixed?** If yes, the refactor is unnecessary.
- **Is the warn a false positive?** Stale test data ≠ real bug. Don't rewrite components to fix phantom warnings.
- **Does the diff match the task scope?** A 250-line component rewrite to fix a console.warn is over-engineering.
- **Would this pass /review-like-michael?** If the answer is "no, too much churn", say so immediately.

**Why:** The user caught a Codex rewrite that violated every established pattern (minimal diffs, no unnecessary rearrangement, don't over-engineer). I said "Correct but invasive" instead of "Reject this — the fix was already in accessors.ts."

**How to apply:** When any external agent produces changes, check them against CLAUDE.md rules BEFORE giving approval. Flag scope creep immediately.
----

---
name: pre-pr-review
description: Verification-first pre-PR review — mechanical checks against the diff, context docs, and schema, ending with a predicted-review simulation
user_invocable: true
---

<skill-prompt>
Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).

Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)

Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)

If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:

- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.
- **Findings closure first.** For every finding from the previous run and every reviewer/bot comment since: re-run the SPECIFIC check that produced it and report fixed / not-fixed / deferred+ticket per item. A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
- Run steps 1–3 mechanically on the delta only, with Step 0's DATA/FRONTEND scoping applied to the delta. Step 4 shrinks to: every new hunk maps to the review feedback or the ticket, and the bot-comment gate on comments the new push attracted.
- Skip re-reading the context docs unless the delta touches DATA/FRONTEND files and they aren't already in context.
- Escape hatch: if the "follow-up" adds new surface (rebase onto a moved base, new feature code, a refactor beyond what was asked), it is not a re-review — run the full sequence on the full PR diff.

## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)

1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.

1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)

Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)

If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:

- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.

A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
